title.narrative: African Union Commission (AUC) Joint Framework Arrangement (JFA) 2024-2027
African Union Commission Joint Framework Arrangement 2024-27

description.narrative:
AU och dess föregångare bildades utifrån övertygelsen att ekonomisk och politisk integration är en nyckel för Afrikas utvecling och för att Afrika ska kunna hävda sig i världen. Sida bedömmer att dessa grundläggande premisser är lika giltiga idag. Afrika behöver mer samarbete för att tackla utmaningarna på kontinenten, inte mindre. AU har mandatet att utveckla det inom-afrikanska samarbetet i de flesta politikområden som fred och säkerhet, handel, migration och många flera. AU:s framgång i att driva genom demokratiska normer, rättsstatsprinciper, respekt för mänskliga rättigheter, mer integrerad handel, att hantera konflikter med mera har betydelse för Sveriges förmåga att utveckla sitt politiska och ekonomiska partnerskap med Afrika.
Joint Framework Arrangement (JFA) är ett ramverk som utvecklades för att hantera givarsamordning och samarbete. Den aktuella JFA:n avser icke-öronmärkta poolade resurser. Syftet med JFA är stödja AU:s förmåga att leverera på sina egna målsättningar.
AU befinner sig för närvarande i en omfattande reformfas som inbegriper olika aspekter hur AU ska blir bättre rustad organisatoriskt, hur den kan göra prioriteringar och hur den finansiella planeringen inklusive budgetering kan bli effektivare. Det ska sägas att reformerna går trögt, besluten är fattade men den politiska viljan och de organisatoriska förutsättningarna att genomföra dessa reformer har delvis saknats. En viktig fråga här är hur medlemsstater kan ta ökat finansiellt ansvar för AU.
JFA stödjer till fullo dessa reformmål. Den poolar resurser från nuvarande nio partners med gemensam rapportering. Dessutom är JFA:n en plattform för att koordinera processer kring resultat, budgetering och uppföljning. Detta tillvägagångssätt fördjupar den institutionella dialogen med AU och sänker transaktionskostnaderna och effektiviserar samarbetet.

The AU and its predecessor were formed on the basis of the conviction that economic and political integration is key to Africa's development and to Africa's ability to assert itself in the world. Sida assesses that these basic premises are just as valid today. Africa needs more cooperation to tackle the challenges on the continent, not less. The AU has the mandate to develop intra-African cooperation in most policy areas such as peace and security, trade, migration and many more. The AU's success in advancing democratic norms, the rule of law, respect for human rights, more integrated trade, managing conflicts, etc., is important for Sweden's ability to develop its political and economic partnership with African.
The Joint Framework Arrangement (JFA) is a framework that was developed to manage multi donor coordination and collaboration. The current JFA refers to unearmarked pooled resources. The purpose of the JFA is to support the AU's ability to deliver on its own objectives.
The AU is currently in a comrehensive reform phase that includes various aspects of how the AU will be better equipped from an organizational point of view, how it can set priorities and how financial planning, including budgeting, can be made more effective.
It should be said that the reforms are going slowly, the decisions have been made, but the political will and the organizational conditions to implement these reforms have been partly lacking. An important question here is how Member States can take greater financial responsibility for the AU.
JFA fully supports these mentioned reforms. It pools resources from nine current partners with unearmarked funding and joint reporting. In addition, the JFA is a platform for coordinating processes around results, budgeting and follow-up. This approach deepens the institutional dialogue with the AU and lowers transaction costs and makes cooperation more efficient.

The overall objective of the intervention is to support AU:s overall goal "An Integrated, Prosperous and Peaceful Africa, driven by its own citizens and representing a dynamic force in the global arena."
Sweden is part of pooled unearmarked fund and coordination mechanism called the Joint Framework Arrangement (JFA). In Februari 2024, the Second Ten Year Implementation Plan (STYIP) was launched. STYIP defines seven strategic objectives (also called moonshots). Sweden will in this stage contribute to Moonshot four, "Africa Resolves conflicts amicably."
This moonshot has the objective to enhance peace and security by working in four areas: 1) identifying risks to peace and security 2) enhance mechanisms to deal with cross cutting peace, security and stability issues 3) silence the guns and militia groups and 4) operationalize the Africa Peace and Security Architechture (APSA).

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
PAPS contributed to Moonshot 3: Public Institutions are more responsive to citizens needs and Moonshot 4: Africa resolves conflicts peacefully for the year 2024. With regards to Moonshot 3, the annual narrative report for 2024 mentions that PAPS has been working on strengthening citizen engagement, such as the development of the draft RECs Roadmap on Citizens Engagement. The idea of this roadmap is to integrate citizen voices into regional policymaking. Another highlight is the launch of 15 electoral observation missions. With regards to Moonshot 4, the report mentions the coordination between AU and RECs through coordination meetings, joint planning retreats and monitoring missions. For example, the 6th midyear coordination meeting between AU and RECs took place in Ghana on July 21, 2024. Another example is the joint meeting between Panel of the Wise and the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS) Committee of Elders on November 2526, 2024. With regards to the Early Warning and Early Response Systems, the report mentions increased collaboration with the AU and the RECs. In addition, the report highlights the mainstreaming of gender, youth and child protection within its governance, peace and security framework.
Sidas comments: PAPS's results need to be understood from the observed general trend away from multilateralism and the tendency of holding on to sovereignty as a shield against further integration in the field of peace and security. One such example is the challenge AU has in operationalizing the Continental Early Warning System (CEWS). CEWS is part of the African Peace and Security Governance Architecture and its establishment is part of the protocol on the Peace and Security Council (article 12). However, Commissioner Bankole referred to the Early Warning to JFA partners on May 17, 2024 as our greatest headache. He was referring to what the Peace and Security Council called in its 1208th meeting on April 16, 2024 a culture of denialism, in which MS and RECs block conflict prevention interventions on grounds of sovereignty. Even though CEWS has a pillar role in APSA, it has been observed that in the reorganisation of PAPS, it has no independent structure. It falls under the directorate Conflict Management. The decision to release information is highly hierarchical, the decision travels from the political officer, the director, the commissioner to finally to the PSC which makes all of its decisions consensually. It is also noted that only three member states (out of 55) have undergone the Country Structural Vulnerability and resilience Assessment, which is a voluntary process that allows a MS to evaluate its structural weaknesses with regards to conflict. These are Ghana (2017), Ivory Coast (2019) and Zambia (2020).
MS engagement in the AU can also be observed by decreasing MS contribution to the AU. The MS contribution to the AU has in 2023 been capped to 200 MUSD which is a reduction of 50 MUSD. The AUC Chairperson at the time, Moussa Faki remarked in his speech of the 45th ordinary session of the Executive Council meeting on July 18, 2024 that AU:s high ambitions and development plans do not resonate with the budget realities. Further, MS contribute on the whole to about 10 percent to the program budget of the AU. With regards to the mainstreaming of gender, youth and child protection, Sidas assessment is in line with the report, that progressive development has been made. The AU has taken active measures to work with the youth issue. For example, the AU has included members of African Youth Ambassadors for Peace and Wise youth members in AU summits, PSC open sessions and in preventive diplomacy missions with regards to elections. The Wise Youth was appointed as a subsidiary to the Panel of Elders and have been appointed between October 2024 to September 2027. A second example is that the development of the AU Continental Framework on Youth, Peace and Security that is a five-year strategy that ended in 2024. A third example is that the AU has hosted regional consultations on African African Youth perspectives on the New Agenda for Peace in collaboration with the Swiss Embassy and Amany in Addis Abeba. However, it must also be noted, as in many other cases including CEWS, there is a large gap between policy and implementation. The PSC meeting on November 1, 2024 (1243rd Meeting) notes in article 2 of the protocol that only two MS, Nigeria and DRC have National Action Plans (NAP) for the Youth, Peace and Security Agenda.
Save the Children has through support from Sida collaborated with the AU to develop and launch a child protection policy for AU:s Peace Support Operations. Sida can also note a gradual improvement in reporting becoming more impact oriented and result focused. The report lists major achievements, major challenges, lessons learned and recommendations. The detailed sections begins with a summary of outcomes. It is also apparent from the dialogue with AU that the intention is to gradually orient itself to more result based reporting. It should also be noted that the current reporting structure is to a large extent organized according to the structure of AMERT, which is AU:s software program for activity based implementation. This system lists activities, the corresponding budget for each activity and corresponding indicators for each activity. It is anticipated that the Result Framework that is currently underway will produce more analytical reporting.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
